title: Check the qualification is recognised (anabin / ZAB)
duration_realistic: before anything else; 1 day if it is in anabin, 2 to 3 months if a ZAB Statement of Comparability is needed
what_happens: Look the student's school-leaving qualification up in anabin (anabin.kmk.org, run by the KMK's Zentralstelle für ausländisches Bildungswesen). Anabin decides whether the certificate gives direct entry, subject-restricted entry, or only Studienkolleg entry, and everything downstream hangs on that answer. Indian applicants normally satisfy this through the APS certificate instead of a separate anabin printout; applicants who are APS-exempt must upload either the anabin confirmation or a ZAB Statement of Comparability with the visa file. If the qualification does not give direct entry, the student is on a Studienkolleg year plus Feststellungsprüfung and a completely different timeline.
the_trap: Counselors check the university's English-language entry table and skip anabin. Anabin, not the university brochure, is what the visa section and uni-assist apply, and an Indian Class XII that the university's marketing page calls 'eligible' can still be Studienkolleg-only in anabin.
exact_quote: APS India applies the evaluation criteria relevant for access to German higher education, including the criteria published in anabin.

title: NEW 2026: the 70 percent Class XII floor and the one-academic-year bridge
duration_realistic: decided by marks already held; the bridge year costs a full extra year
what_happens: APS India published on 23 February 2026 that the anabin evaluation criteria for Indian qualifications were updated with effect from 15 March 2026, applying to admissions from Winter Semester 2026/27 onwards. Two routes survive, both now with a hard floor: Class XII at 70 percent or more of maximum achievable marks plus APS gives subject-restricted admission via Studienkolleg; Class XII at 70 percent or more plus APS plus one successfully completed academic year of a Bachelor's programme at a recognised Indian institution gives direct subject-restricted admission to that field and closely related subjects. The threshold applies regardless of board (CBSE, ISC, state).
the_trap: Two traps. First, a student at 65 to 69 percent who was admissible under the pre-March-2026 criteria is now not admissible at all, and no amount of IELTS or SOP fixes it. Second, the bridge year is subject-locked: one year of B.Com does not open a German engineering Bachelor's. Counselors who sold 'do one year in India then transfer to any German course' in 2025 must re-advise those students.
exact_quote: From Winter Semester 2026/27 onwards, the updated criteria specify a minimum overall score of 70% of the maximum achievable marks in the Indian Class XII certificate.

title: TestAS only if a university actually asks for it
duration_realistic: fixed sittings; 3 weeks to results (digital) or about 4 weeks (paper-based)
what_happens: CORRECTED vs the 2025 chain. TestAS is not a general requirement for Indian applicants and is not part of the Indian APS procedure; g.a.s.t. states it is relevant in India only where an individual German university demands it. It remains genuinely mandatory inside the APS procedure in Vietnam, and is used for grade-plausibility inside the China APS procedure. Where a university does require it, book around the sitting calendar: evaluation takes about three weeks for the digital test and about four weeks for the paper-based one, and the certificate must land before the university deadline, not before the visa appointment.
the_trap: Two opposite errors. Sending every Indian Bachelor applicant to sit TestAS burns 150 EUR and a month for nothing. Assuming nobody needs it misses the handful of programmes that do. Also note the April 2023 APS Class XII checklist still lists 'Copy of TestAS Results' as a document line while the current APS FAQ says it is not mandatory: send the result if the student happens to have one, do not manufacture one.
exact_quote: TestAS is currently not a mandatory component of the APS verification procedure in India.

title: APS certificate
duration_realistic: at least 2 weeks by rule; 4 to 8 weeks typical, longer in peak season and open-ended if the school or board does not reply
what_happens: The Academic Evaluation Centre, part of the Science Section of the German Embassy in New Delhi, verifies Indian academic documents. Fee 18,000 INR, non-refundable once paid, by CCAvenue during registration or bank transfer. Documents go by courier to the APS office at the DLTA Complex, New Delhi; there are no walk-ins. The certificate is issued as a digitally sealed PDF by email and is reusable for later German applications. Exemptions per the German missions in India: PhD/PostDoc, EU or German public-funds scholarship holders, applicants seeking a non-German degree, holders of a non-Indian foreign degree, and holders of an international school-leaving certificate such as the IB.
the_trap: Two live ones. (1) APS will not hold a file open while the student waits for a pending result, and a new evaluation later means a new 18,000 INR payment under the criteria in force at that time, so apply only once the stage that determines the admission pathway is complete. (2) The digital certificate must be submitted as the original unmodified PDF. Renaming, compressing, scanning or merging it into a combined document breaks the seal and the visa section can reject the file. Certificates issued between December 2025 and the April 2026 seal replacement may show a signature warning in Adobe and are still valid.
exact_quote: The verification fee amounts to 18,000/- INR.

title: NEW 2026: dMAT for Indian Master's applicants in the affected fields
duration_realistic: one fixed sitting; about 2 weeks from test to certificate, and it must precede the APS submission
what_happens: CONFIRMED. From the Summer Semester 2027 Master's intake onwards, Indian applicants whose previous degree falls in Engineering, Commerce / Accounting / Finance / Economics, or Business / Management must submit a Digital Master Test certificate together with their APS documents. The dMAT is run by g.a.s.t., not by APS; fee 150 EUR paid at registration on the official dMAT site. For the first cycle, aps-india.de/dmat lists registration opening 29 June 2026, registration closing 15 September 2026, the test on 26 September 2026 and certificates available 12 October 2026. Applicants who completed APS online registration and shipped complete documents before 29 June 2026 are exempt. A low dMAT score does not by itself cause an APS refusal. APS now permits the complete APS application to be lodged before the dMAT certificate is ready so verification can start in parallel.
the_trap: The dMAT sits in front of APS, and APS sits in front of the visa, so it lengthens the whole chain by a full test cycle. The first registration window closes 15 September 2026 - tomorrow at the date of this check - for a 26 September 2026 sitting. A Summer Semester 2027 Master's applicant in an affected field who misses it has no published second sitting to fall back on; check aps-india.de/dmat for the next cycle rather than assuming one exists.
exact_quote: The requirement applies only if the applicant's previous degree falls within one of the affected fields published by APS India and the application relates to the summer semester 2027 intake or a subsequent intake.

title: Language certificate - C1 for the visa, not B2
duration_realistic: 4 to 10 weeks including a retake buffer
what_happens: CHANGED vs the 2025 chain. The German missions in India now state that an applicant entering Bachelor's or Master's degree studies directly generally needs C1, regardless of whether the programme is taught in German or English. B2 English survives only for an English-medium preparatory course; B1 German for a German-medium preparatory course. Accepted providers for India: Goethe-Institut / Max Mueller Bhavan, ÖSD, telc for German; IELTS or an ALTE member for English. A university may still set a lower bar for admission - that does not bind the visa section.
the_trap: Three ways to lose the intake here. (1) Duolingo, Pearson PTE and the TOEFL home edition are explicitly not recognised for applications in India - a student who tested on any of them has no usable certificate. (2) 'Medium of instruction' letters and exemption letters from Indian colleges are explicitly rejected by APS. (3) An offer that says 'English B2 sufficient' does not protect the visa file, because the mission applies its own C1 rule; counselors advising off the university page alone will build a file that fails at the consulate.
exact_quote: If you intend to enter degree studies (Bachelor or Master) right away, generally the required level of knowledge is C1, regardless if the studies are in German or English.

title: uni-assist preliminary review (VPD) or full application
duration_realistic: 4 to 6 weeks stated; 4 to 5 weeks quoted for Asia at this check
what_happens: Most universities will not look at a foreign qualification until uni-assist has evaluated it. Handling fee EUR 75.00 for the first chosen course of study and EUR 30.00 for each additional course in the same semester, payable regardless of outcome, and charged again in full for a new semester. Where a university requires a VPD rather than a full uni-assist application, uni-assist places the VPD in the My assist account and the student must forward it to the university before the university's own deadline. uni-assist's own instruction is to apply at least eight weeks before the deadline.
the_trap: This is still the step that quietly eats the window. The deadline is the university's date, not a uni-assist date, and the VPD must be in the university's hands by it. Starting in June for a 15 July deadline is already late. Sequence it against the other queues too: for an Indian Master's applicant in an affected field the real order is dMAT, then APS, then uni-assist, then the university - roughly five months of serial queueing before any admission letter exists.
exact_quote: You will usually receive your evaluation result in 4 to 6 weeks – counting from the day on which we received your online application form.

title: Apply through the right portal
duration_realistic: by the deadline; often 15 July for winter, 15 January for summer
what_happens: Three possible routes and the programme record names which one applies: the university's own portal, uni-assist, or hochschulstart (Stiftung für Hochschulzulassung) for the nationally restricted subjects - Humanmedizin, Tiermedizin, Zahnmedizin and Pharmazie - and for locally restricted courses inside the DoSV. Note that hochschulstart warns universities may set a single annual application date of 15 January for international applicants, in departure from the rule for German applicants. Some DoSV universities do not work with uni-assist at all, in which case the route is the university direct.
the_trap: Assuming 15 July is the deadline. For international applicants a university may legally run a once-a-year cycle with 15 January as the only date, and many Master's courses and Studienkolleg places close far earlier. Confirm the deadline per programme before building any timeline backwards from it.
exact_quote: Die Hochschulen können aber für ausländische Studienbewerberinnen und Studienbewerber - abweichend von der Regelung für Deutsche - die Vergabe der Studienplätze im Jahresrhythmus sowie als einzigen Bewerbungstermin den 15. Januar vorsehen.

title: Selection stage, where one exists
duration_realistic: several weeks; the DoSV coordination phase runs over multiple weeks
what_happens: Either an aptitude assessment, a restricted-admission ranking, or nothing at all - the programme record says which. Inside hochschulstart's DoSV the universities build ranked lists and offers are distributed across a coordination phase lasting several weeks, followed by a coordinated clearing round (Koordiniertes Nachrücken). For the four nationally restricted subjects, up to 20 percent of places go to advance quotas, one of which is a dedicated foreign-applicant quota - which is how Medicine works for a non-EU applicant, not through the Abitur-best quota.
the_trap: Students treat the coordination phase as dead time and stop checking the DoSV portal. Offers carry a response window; an unanswered offer lapses. And applicants for Medicine, Dentistry, Veterinary Medicine or Pharmacy who apply as if they were competing on grade percentile have misread the quota structure entirely.
exact_quote: Innerhalb der Koordinierungsphase wird durch die Hochschulen ermittelt, ob Sie Zulassungsangebote für Ihre Bewerbungen erhalten können.

title: Admission decision (Zulassungsbescheid)
duration_realistic: after the deadline; typically 4 to 10 weeks
what_happens: The formal admission letter. For the visa file it must be admission to a full-time, in-person degree programme, a Studienkolleg, or a registration confirmation for a preparatory language course. Any outstanding conditions - preparatory college, proof of the language of instruction - have to be stated on the admission letter itself. Nothing in the visa chain can begin before this document exists.
the_trap: A conditional or informal offer, an email saying 'you will be admitted', or admission to an online or part-time programme will not carry a visa file. Conditions must be written on the letter; a condition agreed verbally or in a separate email is invisible to the visa officer and reads as an incomplete admission.
exact_quote: If you have to still fulfill any conditions (for example preparatory college, proof of knowledge of the study language, etc) it has to be noted in the admissions letter.

title: Blocked account (Sperrkonto) or a Verpflichtungserklärung
duration_realistic: 1 to 3 weeks including transfer and blocking confirmation
what_happens: RESOLVED. The figure for 2026 is EUR 11,904 for one year, released at no more than EUR 992 per month. Three independent official sources agree: the Federal Government's Make it in Germany minimum-amounts table gives 'at least EUR 992 net per month (EUR 11,904 per year, in 2026)' for studying under Section 16b AufenthG; the Berlin immigration authority states the same as the 'current value for the year 2026'; and the German missions in India checklist names EUR 11,904 with an EUR 992 monthly cap. The 2024 figure of EUR 992 per month took effect on 1 September 2024 and has not moved since. The alternatives are a Verpflichtungserklärung signed by a sponsor resident in Germany before that sponsor's local immigration office, or proof of a German or EU scholarship; an education loan should be evidenced as well. Related amounts differ: the university-place-seeker visa under Section 17(2) and the opportunity card under Section 20a both require EUR 1,091 per month in 2026, not EUR 992.
the_trap: Do not quote EUR 10,332. That is the 2023 figure, and the DAAD-run study-in-germany.de portal was still publishing it as 'currently 10,332 euros annually' on the date of this check - a stale official page that costs students a rejected file. Second trap: the blocking confirmation must state the monthly withdrawal cap, not just the balance. A plain bank statement showing EUR 11,904 is not a Sperrkonto and will not be accepted.
exact_quote: For a stay for study purposes, a monthly amount of 992.00 euros must be available, i.e. 11,904.00 euros per year (current value for the year 2026).

title: Health insurance from the date of arrival
duration_realistic: 3 to 10 days
what_happens: CHANGED vs the 2025 chain. The German missions in India now ask for a certificate of compulsory health insurance - statutory or comparable private - effective from the intended date of arrival in Germany, rather than a 90-day travel policy. The older September 2024 mission checklist still lists travel health insurance covering the first 90 days, so carry both if the enrolment date is later than arrival. Statutory cover (TK, AOK, Barmer and others) costs roughly EUR 120 to 130 per month for students under 30; at 30 the student rate ends and the standard contribution applies. EU, EEA and Swiss students can generally rely on an EHIC plus a German insurer's certificate of exemption from compulsory insurance.
the_trap: Foreign health insurance is not sufficient - the Berlin immigration authority says so in terms, and an Indian policy or a parent's employer cover will not carry either the visa or the enrolment. Opting into private cover is close to irreversible: a student who takes private insurance normally cannot switch to statutory insurance later in the degree.
exact_quote: Certificate about compulsory health insurance (Gesetzliche oder private Krankenversicherung) from the intended date of arrival in Germany.

title: Budget the semester contribution and any state tuition
duration_realistic: decided before the application, paid at enrolment and again every semester
what_happens: CONFIRMED. The semester contribution is charged by every German higher education institution and runs between EUR 70 and EUR 430 per semester; it funds the Studierendenwerk and the student body and usually includes a semester transport ticket, at some universities the nationwide Deutschlandticket. Separately, Baden-Württemberg charges non-EU citizens EUR 1,500 per semester in tuition for Bachelor's, Master's, Diplom and state-examination programmes (doctoral students excepted), and Bavarian institutions may set their own fees for non-EU/EEA students. Private universities charge their own fees, and the mission will want proof that the first year or a substantial deposit has been paid.
the_trap: 'Study in Germany is free' is only true for the public universities in the other fourteen states. A student who picks Stuttgart, Karlsruhe, Heidelberg or Freiburg on the strength of that phrase is signing up for EUR 3,000 a year that was never in the budget - and the blocked account of EUR 11,904 is for living costs and does not cover it.
exact_quote: The semester contribution varies between higher education institutions and comes to between 70 and 430 EUR.

title: NEW 2026: complete the online application in the Consular Services Portal first
duration_realistic: 1 to 2 weeks to assemble and upload; the appointment link only appears at the end
what_happens: CHANGED vs the 2025 chain, and this reverses the old order. 'Study purposes and seeking a university place' is one of the visa types available in the Federal Foreign Office's Consular Services Portal at digital.diplo.de, and where the CSP offers a type the online application is obligatory. The portal starts with a questionnaire that routes the applicant into a sub-type; wrong answers cannot be edited and force a delete-and-restart. Everything is uploaded inside the portal - passport data page, school or degree certificates with all semester mark sheets, language certificate, APS certificate, admission letter, motivation letter, tabular CV, proof of funds, health insurance certificate, and proof of paid fees for a private university or language course. Residence, not citizenship, decides the responsible mission; an Indian citizen living in Dubai applies to the UAE, not India.
the_trap: This is the single biggest procedural change in the chain. The old advice - 'book the VFS appointment the moment admission lands' - is now wrong: the appointment link is issued only at the end of a completed and pre-checked CSP application. A student who books a slot without completing the CSP upload will be turned away on the day and loses the slot, and slots are the scarcest thing in the process. The questionnaire also asks about German at B2: answer yes only if the student genuinely has German B2, otherwise the whole application has to be deleted and restarted.
exact_quote: Only then will you receive a link to book an on-site-appointment at the end of the process.

title: Book and attend the on-site appointment (VFS)
duration_realistic: highly variable; a chronological waiting list rather than a bookable calendar in peak season
what_happens: With the CSP link, the student books the on-site biometric and document appointment at the VFS centre responsible for their place of residence and attends with originals of everything uploaded. The visa fee is EUR 75 / 8,400 INR for applicants over 18 and EUR 37.50 / 4,200 INR for under-18s, paid in rupees at the day's rate, plus a separate VFS service fee; the fee is not refunded on refusal or withdrawal. Fee waivers exist for holders of a public-funds scholarship.
the_trap: The German missions in India run a chronological waiting list, not an open calendar, and have said in terms that the upcoming winter semester is not a valid reason for a special appointment - and that emailing to ask for one slows everyone down. Register the moment the CSP application is complete and then leave it alone. Do not let a student book at the wrong mission: choosing a mission not responsible for their state gets the application deleted, not transferred.
exact_quote: The upcoming winter semester is not a valid reason for granting a special appointment.

title: Visa processing and the decision
duration_realistic: 6 to 8 weeks officially; 3 to 6 months from APS start to visa in hand
what_happens: The mission forwards the file to the competent foreigners authority in Germany, which is why the stated processing time is six to eight weeks rather than days; the missions decline status enquiries in the first three months. The national visa is normally issued for 90 days up to a year and permits travel in the Schengen area for 90 days in any 180. Counting dMAT or TestAS where they apply, APS, uni-assist, admission, the CSP application, the appointment wait and processing, the realistic span from starting the file to landing in Germany is three to six months - which is how a 15 July deadline becomes a very tight October start.
the_trap: Remonstration has been abolished in India since 1 January 2024. A refusal no longer has a cheap internal appeal; the only stated remedy is a lawsuit at the administrative court in Berlin. That makes the first submission the only realistic submission, and it is why the C1 rule, the unmodified APS PDF and the blocking confirmation all have to be right the first time.
exact_quote: As your application will be forwarded to the competent Aliens' Authorities in Germany, the processing of your application will take six to eight weeks.

title: Find accommodation with a Wohnungsgeberbestätigung
duration_realistic: start 3 months out; in Munich, Berlin and Frankfurt expect it to run past arrival
what_happens: Rarely treated as a step, and it gates the two after it. Municipal registration requires either a tenancy agreement or the landlord's written confirmation that the student has moved in - the Wohnungsgeberbestätigung - and the landlord is legally obliged to supply it within two weeks of move-in. Short lets, hostels and most Airbnbs will not issue one. Studierendenwerk halls are the reliable route and several bundle health insurance into a service package.
the_trap: A student arrives on a room booked through a sublet that cannot give a Wohnungsgeberbestätigung, so cannot register, so cannot open a bank account or apply for the residence permit, and the 90-day visa runs out during the search. Confirm in writing that the landlord will issue the form before paying any deposit.
exact_quote: Tenancy agreement or confirmation from your landlord that you have moved in

title: 2026: the Entry/Exit System (EES) and the visa-free 90/180 clock
duration_realistic: extra time at the border on first entry; the 90/180 allowance is now counted automatically
what_happens: The EU's digital Entry/Exit System became fully operational on 10 April 2026 at the external borders of every EU member state except Cyprus and Ireland, plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland. It records fingerprints and a facial image on first entry and logs entries and exits digitally in place of passport stamping. It matters for track b - nationals who may enter visa-free and then apply for the residence permit inside Germany - because their 90-days-in-180 allowance is now machine-counted rather than read off stamps. Students entering on a national Type D visa (tracks c and d) are exempt, as are EU, EEA and Swiss nationals and holders of residence permits. Separately, Indian nationals no longer need an airport transit visa when connecting through a German airport, in force since 3 June 2026.
the_trap: Track b students used to rely on ambiguous or missing stamps to blur the 90-day limit. That is over: the clock is exact, and it is the same clock the foreigners authority uses to judge whether the residence permit application was made in time. Any prior short Schengen trip in the preceding 180 days eats into the allowance before the student even lands to study. First-entry biometric enrolment also lengthens the border queue, so build a buffer into a tight onward connection.
exact_quote: Exempt from this requirement are, among others, citizens of the EU , the EEA and Switzerland, in addition to holders of residence permits and visas for long-term stays.

title: Register the address (Anmeldung)
duration_realistic: within 2 weeks of moving in; add appointment waiting time in large cities
what_happens: In person at the Bürgeramt or Einwohnermeldeamt with passport, visa and the landlord's confirmation. Registration itself is free. The Meldebescheinigung that comes out of it is the key to everything administrative afterwards - the residence permit, a German bank account, a mobile contract. EU, EEA and Swiss students receive their proof of right of residence here rather than at the foreigners authority.
the_trap: Students prioritise the university over the Bürgeramt and lose weeks. In Berlin and Munich the appointment itself has a queue, so book it before flying rather than after arriving, and remember the two-week clock starts at move-in, not at landing.
exact_quote: Most important is registering at the residents' registration office. You cannot, for example, open a bank account until you have done this.

title: Enrol at the university (Immatrikulation)
duration_realistic: a short fixed window at the start of the semester
what_happens: At the Studentensekretariat, usually in person on a set date, sometimes by post within a deadline. Documents: passport with visa or residence permit, the admission letter, and proof of statutory health insurance in Germany. The semester contribution of EUR 70 to 430 is paid here and again before every subsequent semester. Enrolment also brings automatic accident cover through the institution. The Immatrikulationsbescheinigung that results is what the foreigners authority asks for.
the_trap: Enrolment windows are short and unforgiving, and they are the reason the whole chain is timed. Missing the window means waiting a semester with a visa already issued. Re-registration each semester is equally hard-edged: miss it and the student can be de-registered, which also invalidates the basis of the residence permit.
exact_quote: Only once you have enrolled can you attend courses at your higher education institution, take exams and gain an academic degree.

title: Convert to a residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis, Section 16b)
duration_realistic: apply before the visa expires; the card itself can take several months to arrive
what_happens: CHANGED vs the 2025 chain: at a growing number of foreigners authorities, Berlin included, this now starts as an online application with the fee paid up front by card or PayPal, and the in-person interview is granted only after the file has been checked. Documents: passport and visa, certificate of enrolment or admission, the registration certificate, proof of funds at the EUR 992 per month level, and proof of German health insurance. Fee up to EUR 100 - Berlin charges EUR 100 for the electronic residence permit (eAT) and EUR 56 for a sticker. The permit is generally granted for two years and renewed for two, subject to the authority being satisfied the student is progressing. It allows 140 full days or 280 half-days of work per calendar year, or 20 hours a week in term, raised from 120/240 by the Skilled Immigration Act. After graduation the student can stay 18 months to look for qualified work.
the_trap: Students who entered visa-free (track b) must apply within 90 days of entry; Berlin's own wording is that residence stays lawful pending a decision only if the first application is made fewer than 91 days after arrival. Track c and d students must apply before the D visa expires, not before the semester starts - the visa can be as short as 90 days. Submitting the online application produces a PDF confirmation that extends the validity of the existing title: save and print it, because it is the only proof of lawful stay while the eAT card is being produced. Note also that the Chancenkarte (opportunity card, Section 20a) is a job-search route requiring EUR 1,091 per month and a recognised qualification - it is not a study route and should not be offered as a shortcut into a German degree.
exact_quote: The residence permit is generally granted and extended for two years. It entitles the holder to work for a total of 140 full work days in a calendar year.
